title: Dachepalli Publishers Ltd - 544667 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 total income rose 159% YoY to INR45.18 crore, with PAT up 42% to INR6.3 crore, though management attributes margin compression to raw-material timing.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR45.18 crore (up 159% YoY), EBITDA of INR9.2 crore (up 31%) and PAT of INR6.3 crore (up 42%). Q1 revenue mix was about INR30 crore textbooks and INR15 crore via the Pelican Edu Supply e-commerce channel. Analysts pressed on receivables rising to about INR100 crore and EBITDA margin falling from about 40% to 20% YoY; management blamed raw-material invoicing timing. FY27 turnover guidance was cut to a range of INR130-150 crore in one answer, while other answers cited INR220-250 crore, and the company gave no clear reconciliation.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin (Q1, as cited by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: down from about 40% YoY per analyst question; management did not dispute the figure
up from about INR75 crore in March

segments.name: Textbooks (direct/distributor)
segments.commentary: About INR30 crore of Q1 sales, sold through distributors to schools. Management says the B2B:B2C mix stays around 70:30.

segments.name: Pelican Edu Supply (school-linked e-commerce)
segments.commentary: About INR15 crore of Q1 sales, paid upfront. Tied up with about 50 schools in FY27, with 100+ schools tied up for next year and 50-60 in pipeline. Management says it is about 30% of projected FY27 turnover.

segments.name: Notebooks and stationery
segments.commentary: Notebook manufacturing machinery acquired, shifting from trading to in-house production; current machines support about 10-20% of demand in covered markets. Stationery is currently traded (Doms, Nataraj, Camlin), with white-labelling planned at 15,000-18,000 units per item.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover estimate given as INR130-150 crore in one answer, and as INR130-140 crore by Q4 in another; INR220-250 crore cited for FY27 as a longer-range target.
Management estimates PAT margin of about 17-18%, which it says it held in the prior year as well.
Receivables expected to be about 90% recovered by October-November; 40-50% collected in July.
Five-year plan includes Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore) exports after stronger domestic share.
Market share in newly entered states (UP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam) is about 1-2%, targeted at 5% in three years.
capex_capacity: Textbook printing machines at 80-85% utilisation; existing capacity adequate up to about INR300 crore turnover.
Notebook machines currently cover only about 10-20% of demand in covered markets; further machine purchases planned as notebook volumes grow.
Notebook manufacturing machinery acquired in Q1, marking backward integration from trading to in-house production.
Capex and warehousing funded from internal accruals before listing, per management.
demand_pricing: Schools supplied: about 13,000 for textbooks; 50 schools on the e-commerce tool. Coverage 10,000-12,000 schools cited earlier.
Average ticket size per school rose from about INR1 lakh to about INR40 lakh after the direct-to-parent model, per management.
Free LMS/AI platform offered to schools, with textbook MRP raised by INR10-12 (on a INR200 maths book) to recover cost.
Market share is about 1% in new states versus higher in the South; Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are the strongest states.
Receivables build-up is seasonal: schools reopen around June 15-18, and most collections come in July to October.

qa_highlights.question: Why have trade receivables risen from about INR75 crore to about INR100 crore, and how much is over six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales are booked in Q4 and Q1, 40%+ of the INR100 crore was recovered by July, and about 90% is expected by October-November. It said 90% of payments are recovered within six months, with 7-10% blocked.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 40% to 20% YoY in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw-material purchases were invoiced after April 1 this year, while last year they were booked in Q4 FY26. It said full-year margins should normalise, and that raw material hits the P&L on vendor invoice regardless of sale.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 on track for about INR250 crore revenue and INR25 crore PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects INR130-140 crore turnover by Q4, and that Pelican could add 50-60 pipeline schools, which would take FY27 to INR220+ crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce share of revenue and will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30% of the current year's estimated INR130 crore turnover comes from e-commerce, and that the 70:30 split will hold next year while absolute business grows.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the 159% growth and what is the strategy in new states?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prescribed textbooks last 3-4 years in a school, so orders are multi-year. It targets raising market share from about 1-2% to 5% in new states over three years, with UP the largest opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and capex outlook as new businesses scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated PAT margin of about 17-18% and said most cost variability now comes from raw materials, with existing capex already in place. Notebook machine purchases would follow demand growth.

risks_watch: Receivables of about INR100 crore at Q1 end; management says 7-10% may be blocked beyond six months, which needs verification against the balance sheet.
Q1 EBITDA margin of about 20% versus about 40% a year earlier; management attributes this to timing, but it needs confirmation in Q2 and Q3 numbers.
FY27 guidance is inconsistent across answers (INR130-140 crore, INR130-150 crore, INR220-250 crore); clarity is needed.
Dependence on textbook prescriptions and curriculum changes; management says changes are minor yearly but three full revisions have happened since independence.
Pelican Edu Supply scale-up is slow (50 to 100-150 schools) and operationally complex, so the INR40 lakh ticket-size claim needs tracking.
Competition from edtech and from other publishers that may also offer free technology.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and multi-year school contracts, but defensive when questioned on margins and receivables. Management repeatedly framed weakness as seasonal or timing-related, and some guidance figures were inconsistent across answers.
key_quotes: Actually, the gross margin has not declined, sir.
But overall profit of the company will go on to be remain the same 17% or 18% which has happened last year also.
So, 90% of the payments will be recovered before six months only.
So, technology keeps building over time every year whatever new is coming, we are also getting adopted into our technology.

growth.why: FY27 turnover guidance is inconsistent: INR130-150 crore (cut to INR130-140 crore by Q4 in one answer) versus INR220-250 crore cited elsewhere, with no reconciliation; Q1 revenue up 159% and EBITDA up 31% but EBITDA margin reportedly fell from about 40% to 20%, and receivables rose to about INR100 crore, so guidance is not clearly backed by orders or capacity.
